title: Four Easy Tricks to Help You Eat Better
paragraphs: Eating healthily can be difficult, but small changes can make a big difference. Here are four easy tricks that may help you eat better.

The same amount of food looks bigger on a smaller plate. According to Pierre Chandon, a researcher who studies food choices, a plate or cup that is about 10% to 20% smaller than usual works best, because people do not really notice the difference.
2. Keep healthy food where you can see it

People often eat the food that is easiest to see and reach. So, try putting fruit on the kitchen table or at the front of your fridge, and keep less healthy snacks out of sight. It can also help to cut up fruit and vegetables in advance and store them in the fridge. This way, they are ready to eat when you feel hungry.

According to the UK's National Health Service (NHS), it takes about 20 minutes for your stomach to tell your brain that you are full. If you eat too quickly, you may eat more than you need. To slow down, take smaller bites, chew your food well and put down your fork between bites. The NHS also suggests that you stop eating before you feel too full.
Before you go to the supermarket, make a list of the healthy foods you need for the week. Having a plan can help you avoid buying unhealthy snacks on impulse.
Remember that no single trick will work like magic for everyone. However, small habits like these can make healthy choices easier every day.
